summary: Players bid on action cards to acquire goods for a personal warehouse, then race to assemble the exact cargo a harbor ship demands before it fills and sails; the signature 'extortion' mechanic has one player set price/terms that an opponent then chooses which side of. It was an unexpected buzz title at Essen Spiel 2007 and got a Golden Geek nomination, but some found it fiddly to teach.
praised: Surprisingly deep, tense decision-making for a small card game
The forced-choice extortion bidding mechanic, called 'agonizing and incredibly rewarding' by longtime fans
Was a standout buzz title at Essen Spiel 2007 and a 2008 Golden Geek Best Card Game nominee
criticised: Some reviewers found it demanding/fiddly to teach new players
The mean, forced extortion mechanic is divisive — loved by some, off-putting to others

interaction.detail: The harbor with its limited ship slots is a shared, contested space, but each player also keeps a private warehouse of goods. Interaction is direct: a player sets price/terms on a deal and an opponent is forced to pick which side of it they get stuck with, actively shaping rivals' outcomes rather than just competing indirectly.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The only thing that actually scores is successfully loading a ship with the exact combination of goods it demands before it sails.
scoring.how_you_win: Win auctions to stock your warehouse with the right goods, then deliver a complete matching cargo to a ship before it departs; whoever completes the most valuable deliveries has the most points when the fleet is gone.
